textbookBox.concept: An identity is an equation that is true for all values of the variables, unlike an ordinary equation that is true only for some values.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: An identity is an equation that is true for all values of the variables, unlike an ordinary equation that is true only for some values.
beats.speakEn: An identity is an equation that is true for all values of the variables, unlike an ordinary equation that is true only for some values.

beats.en: Cutting a square of side (a + b) into pieces gives (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2.
beats.speakEn: Cutting a square of side (a + b) into pieces gives (a + b)^2  equals  a^2 + 2ab + b^2.

type: Key Concept: An identity is an equation that is true for all values of the variables, unlike an ordinary
Rule: Cutting a square of side (a + b) into pieces gives (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 9 maths · Exploring Algebraic Identities · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Replacing b by -b gives (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2.

beats.en: Replacing b by -b gives (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2.
beats.speakEn: Replacing b by -b gives (a - b)^2  equals  a^2 - 2ab + b^2.

beats.en: The difference of squares identity is a^2 - b^2 = (a + b)(a - b). A rectangle cut and rearranged shows it.
beats.speakEn: The difference of squares identity is a^2 - b^2  equals  (a + b)(a - b). A rectangle cut and rearranged shows it.

type: Replacing b by -b gives (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2.
The difference of squares identity is a^2 - b^2 = (a + b)(a - b).
